newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mystery buyer raids Australia's Burns Philp.
newsitem.headline: Mystery buyer raids Australia's Burns Philp.

text.p: A mystery buyer launched a surprise raid on Australian spices and yeast group Burns Philp & Co on Friday, buying a 14-percent stake and sparking speculation of an imminent takeover bid.

Broker Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said on Friday it had bought 78.16 million shares in spices and yeast group Burns Philp & Co Ltd at A$2.50 (US$1.88) a share for a client that was not an international food group.
The DMG offer price was 47 cents or 23 percent above Burns' A$2.03 closing price on Thursday.
DMG director Robin Yandle told Reuters he would be active in the stock again later on Friday either as a buyer or a seller, depending on the price.
"We've bought 78.16 million shares or 14 percent of Burns Philp, all at A$2.50 a share, from a range of sellers, both domestic and international," Yandle said.
He said there had been 40 sellers and one buyer.

Yandle confirmed that the buyer was not an international food group and that he considered Australia's Goodman Fielder Ltd -- rumoured to be mulling a takeover bid -- to be an international food group.
He said the client was an overseas-based individual that does not have any food assets at this stage but would not otherwise comment on individual names.
The Australian Financial Review said some institutions believed the mystery buyer was a wealthy New Zealander, possibly Ron Brierley and his Guiness Peat Group Plc.
The Sydney Morning Herald said Deutsche Morgan had acted in the past for international investor George Soros.
DMG's description of the buyer would also exclude Burns Philp's major U.S. competitor McCormick and Co Inc.
Burns' share price rocketed to the DMG offer price in early trade on the Australian Stock Exchange, but had eased back to A$2.40 by 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT).
Burns Philp itself said it did not know of any takeover bid for the group or the identity of the buyer.
"There's no information we have we can pass on to the stock exchange," the spokesman said.

Burns' share price has lagged a booming Australian market this year as it continued to disappoint investors with below expectation earnings from its U.S., European and Australian spice and yeast operations.
Burns, under pressure from increasingly disgruntled shareholders, announced last month it would sell its herb and spice businesses to focus on its yeast activities.
The company also announced the retirement of managing director Ian Clack.
